Safety Dashawn Spears suffered an ACL injury against the Ole Miss Rebels, which has ruled him out for the rest of the season, opening up the star safety position in the secondary. Safety Tamarcus Cooley has taken over the position for Spears and is expected to stay in the role for the rest of the season. Linebacker Charles Ross is also out for the season after suffering a torn ACL vs. Texas A&M. Ross was listed behind Weeks on LSU's depth chart before Weeks' injury. As linebacker Davhon Keys has stepped in for Weeks, there are still fewer options in the position room for backups. Here's my North Dakota State vs. UNLV prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 10. North Dakota State vs. UNLV Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5 My UNLV vs. North Dakota State best bet is on the Rebels' total points. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download our Action Network app to get the latest picks and betting analysis. North Dakota State vs UNLV Odds North Dakota State vs UNLV point spread : North Dakota State -3.5 (-102), UNLV +3.5 (-120) North Dakota State vs UNLV over/under : 48.5 (-105o / -115u) North Dakota State vs UNLV moneyline : North Dakota State -160, UNLV +130 North Dakota State has been impressive this season in its first at the FBS level, and the transition has gone as well as anyone would have predicted. The Bison are 5-0 both straight up and against the spread, led by their defense, which is tied with Miami for first in the country. NDSU has allowed just 9.8 points per game this season. The Bison have remained true to the identity that brought them so much success at the FCS level, using a ball-control offense, power running game and rock-solid defense to win games. The offense isn't as explosive, dominant or dynamic as in previous seasons, but quarterback Nathan Hayes has completed 65% of his passes with 995 yards through the air and a 7:2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. The ground game has been effective and efficient without being overly explosive. NDSU is averaging 171 rushing yards per game as a team on 4.2 yards per carry. DJ Scott and Myles Mitchell garner the majority of the carries and have rushed for 512 yards between the pair with seven combined rushing scores. Jackson Williams is the most consistent receiver and has hauled in 22 passes for 358 yards this season. He'll see a decent amount of the target share in this game. The defense has been unbelievably impressive while holding four of its five opponents to 10 points or less. The Bison have been strong against the run and have held their opponents — including Air Force — to just three yards per carry and 102 yards per game on the ground. The secondary hasn't surrendered explosive plays, and only 40% of opponent red-zone trips have resulted in touchdowns. This bunch will have its hands full against UNLV on the road this week, but I expect a decent showing out of this defense. UNLV has to consider this season mildly disappointing thus far, as the Rebels dropped the season opener at home against Memphis and were embarrassed on the road at North Texas earlier in the season. Recently, however, the offense has come to life with back-to-back games, scoring 38 and 39 points in wins over Akron and Cal . The Rebels have their sights set on continuing to remain in contention for a Mountain West title. The offense is going to remain run-oriented, as Jai'Den Thomas leads the way with 383 yards and a pair of rushing scores. Thomas provides explosiveness and versatility out of the running back position and is a great complement to quarterback Jackson Arnold , who has run for 270 yards while leading the team with five rushing scores. Arnold has thrown the ball well over the last two weeks, and connecting on the downfield passes has spring-loaded the scoring for UNLV. While only 59% of his passes have been completed, Arnold creates well on the move, has thrown eight touchdown passes without an interception, and many of his incomplete passes were throwaways to avoid sacks. The eyesore has been the offensive line, which has surrendered 14 sacks and 28 tackles for loss. This group will have its work cut out for them against a strong Bison defensive front. The UNLV defense isn't a strong unit, but it has played well at times this season. Holding Hawaii to six points on the road was quite a feat, and Akron was held scoreless after halftime a couple of weeks back. Cal scored 31 points last week against this defense in completely fluky fashion. One scoring drive was a 91-yard touchdown pass where a defender fell, and another missed a tackle. After halftime, UNLV surrendered a scoring drive of 52 yards, followed up by fumbling the ensuing kickoff. The offense has run a slower tempo recently and will likely do so here to keep the defense fresh, but this stop unit will have to be rock-solid in order to see UNLV compete with NDSU. This game has North Dakota State listed as a 3.5-point road favorite with a total set at 48.5. This total has been bet down from 51.5 on the opener. I agree with the move and feel this matchup is one between even teams. I'm willing to take NDSU's team total under 25.5. This game will be played at a very slow pace, and the Bison will operate very slowly when they have the ball. While this offense has put up a decent amount of points this season, the strength of schedule disparity in this matchup is monumental. North Dakota State has feasted on weak defenses, including Sac State , Fordham and Air Force . The Rebs have controlled the line of scrimmage this season and have done well to prevent explosives on the ground. NDSU won't find the chunk plays on the ground in this game, and I wouldn't be surprised to see UNLV get the Bison off the field early in this game until they settle in. The Rebels have given up some explosiveness through the air, something NDSU is ill-equipped to exploit in this matchup. UNLV has an excellent red-zone defense that has allowed just eight touchdowns on 17 attempts. I look for the UNLV stop unit to bow up in the red area and force NDSU to settle for field goals, something we've seen in recent weeks. The Rebels will run the ball a decent amount, and while they'll be effective, they won't be explosive. NDSU has made a concerted effort defensively to keep everything in front of it, and the defense forces long, methodical drives. UNLV's performance in the red zone has been terrible this season, as only 53% of trips have resulted in touchdowns, and the Rebs gamble on fourth-and-goal a lot. Doing that again will leave NDSU with long fields, so the Bison will take time off the clock on long, methodical drives. I think this game will be a lower-scoring competitive grind, with the winning team not surpassing 24 total points. This is a tough trip against a team that has played a much tougher schedule to date, so I will bet that the Bison offense struggles for the first time this season. Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5

picks.headline: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown
picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia operates a committee-style running back room, and Smart keeps saying that Georgia will continue to spread the football around. Frazier is still the lead back, and he will have his touches increased in big games. Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Bryce Young, Nick Saban, ESPN's College GameDay Make Picks For Alabama-Georgia Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS BAMA FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM ALABAMA BASKETBALL NEWS ESPN's College GameDay chose Tuscaloosa to host this week's pregame show as No. 6 Alabama is facing No. 2 Georgia at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC . The analysts on College GameDay closed the three-hour morning show from Coleman Coliseum by picking the winner of this top-10 SEC showdown. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban is one of the analysts, alongside Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and host Rece Davis. They are also joined by a celebrity guest each week, with Saturday's being former Alabama and current Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young . So, which panelists picked Alabama over Georgia, and how many chose the Bulldogs over the Crimson Tide? Note: Davis, the host, doesn't make picks, and the same is said for Herbstreit, who is on the call tonight. Desmond Howard: Alabama Nick Saban: Alabama Bryce Young: Alabama Pat McAfee: Georgia Saban : "You know, I think Georgia's got one of the most complete teams in the country. I love Kirby, he's had a very consistent identity with his teams — tough, physical and all of that. But I really like the togetherness of Alabama's team this year, so I'm going Roll Tide, baby." Young : "Seeing how well a team plays together here at Bama, watching the togetherness, the secondary gelling with all of the turnovers they're creating, and I think the X-factor is Keelon Russell. Watching him develop, watching how well he's playing, watching him have command, I'm a huge fan, I think he's super special. So, of course, Roll Tide." Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer joined the College GameDay set for a segment earlier in the show and was asked if there's something that the college football world doesn't see that makes him believe in the Crimson Tide. UA started the season ranked No. 13 in the AP Top 25, but is now 5-0 and the No. 6 team in the renowned poll. "There’s a third field that we don’t practice as much on, but it’s where the grind happened in the offseason. And I think just the lessons learned and the things that we went through, the guys have this belief and trust because they know that everyone’s doing the work." Alabama's Practice Field 3 was a staple of the summer, and BamaCentral spoke with nine different Crimson Tide players about the haunting workouts that occurred there. Alabama leads the all-time series against Georgia 45-27-4, with the first matchup occurring on Nov. 2, 1895. The Crimson Tide has a 24-13-4 home record against the Bulldogs and has won eight of the past 10 overall meetings. However, Georgia has had the last laugh, beating the Crimson Tide 28-7 in the 2025 SEC Championship Game. Alabama finished with -3 rushing yards and was without multiple key players. It was just the second time that season, with the other being the previous Oklahoma matchup, that the Alabama defense did not force a turnover. One of the biggest games of the college football season is at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., today at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) when Georgia and Alabama play for the 10th time in the Kirby Smart era. Alabama is the 2.5-point favorite with a 53% win probability. The Crimson Tide are 1.5-point home favorites with College GameDay in town, and given Smart's struggles against them, my Georgia vs. Alabama prediction and Week 6 college football picks project Kalen DeBoer's program to win a defensive battle in the downpour. This updates my early Georgia vs. Alabama prediction . Who will win Georgia vs Alabama today? Pick: Alabama ML Kirby Smart has historically struggled against Alabama , and I like the Crimson Tide to cover up to -1.5 , but would rather play it safe and take the Tide to win. Since taking over Georgia in 2017, Smart is 2-7 straight up against the Crimson Tide and 0-3 in the regular season since 2020. With the Georgia vs. Alabama weather report calling for heavy rain and strong winds, this game will likely be low-scoring and come down to which offense can make more explosive plays late. That gives the Crimson Tide the advantage, with Keelon Russell ranking third nationally in QBR (91.0) and Alabama's offense being 12th in the country in offensive success rate (51.2%). Georgia's defense hasn't faced an offense as loaded as Alabama's this season. Our Week 6 college football AI predictions also have Alabama winning, 37-30. And against the lone quality defense Georgia QB Gunner Stockton has faced ( Oklahoma ), he struggled (65.7 QBR, 60.9% adjusted completion rate). College GameDay even announced it's relocating this morning's show inside due to the weather in Tuscaloosa. There's an 83% chance of precipitation with wind gusts of 19 mph at kickoff, which will only help these defenses shine. That will change this weekend, as the Bulldogs will need Gunner Stockton’s arm to make plays on the road. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunnar Stockton (14). It's the game of the week between Georgia and Alabama, and we've got plenty of player props to break down ahead of this heated SEC showdown, with a tropical storm adding another wrinkle to the matchup. Weather aside, I dug through the board and found three props I believe are well worth a look. Without further ado, here are my Georgia vs. Alabama prop picks , headlined by another big outing from Bulldogs quarterback Gunnar Stockton. Before you get too far, be sure to check out all of our college football picks for Week 6. Best Georgia vs Alabama props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Under 238.5 passing yards Despite my belief that Georgia will come out on top in this matchup, Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell will likely struggle through the air in Week 6, even if he's forced to play from behind. We've already seen him struggle against a semi-competent pass defense this season, as he managed just 188 passing yards against Kentucky. The Wildcats rank 74th nationally in passing yards allowed per game but surrender just 6.0 yards per attempt, the 16th-best mark in the country. Georgia is allowing just 209.3 passing yards per game this season , ranking 53rd nationally. While the Bulldogs haven't faced top-tier competition, the Crimson Tide have yet to encounter a defense of this caliber. If the Bulldogs want to pull off the upset in Tuscaloosa, they'll need to limit the Crimson Tide's aerial attack, making Russell's Under 238.5 passing yards worth a look. Playable down to 230 yards. Prop pick #2: Gunner Stockton Over 199.5 passing yards Georgia hasn't leaned heavily on its passing game early this season, with just 44.53% of its plays coming through the air. And rightfully so, as all five of its wins have come by 24 or more points. However, this matchup should be far more competitive and could be one of the toughest tests of the season for both teams. Gunner Stockton has surpassed 199.5 passing yards three times this season. In the other two games, the Bulldogs largely had things wrapped up by halftime, eliminating the need to air it out or prompting them to bring in the backup. This matchup should require Stockton to play all four quarters, and with the spread suggesting Georgia could be playing from behind, the senior QB may need to air it out. The Crimson Tide have allowed more than 230 passing yards per game this season , with opponents averaging 7.6 yards per attempt. That presents a solid opportunity for Stockton to clear 199.5 passing yards. And for those SPRINTING to @ me on X about the weather, The Weather Channel forecasts the storm to pass by kickoff, with just a 24% chance of precipitation and winds of 7-9 mph. SLING THAT PILL, GUNNER! Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 20.5 rushing yards With sacks counting against a college quarterback's rushing yards, Russell's longest rush prop is worth a look. All of his longest runs this season have gone for more than 15 yards, even against Kentucky, when he finished with -9 rushing yards. That line should hover around 13.5 yards. Russell has used his legs plenty early this season, rushing for more than 35 yards in three of Alabama's five games. His season-high came against East Carolina, when he ran for 86 yards. With the pressure Georgia's defense will bring against the sophomore quarterback, Russell will likely be forced out of the pocket and looking for open grass. Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. Cole opened the season with a half-sack, and added anther against Oklahoma with two fumble recoveries. Cole had 60 tackles last season, ranking fourth, and a team-leading 4.5 sacks. Cole has 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks to this season. Last year, Cole had five tackles versus Alabama and a sack. Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. #6 Alabama Crimson Tide Head Coach: Kalen DeBoer 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 49.6 (2nd) Defensive Points Per Game: 20.8 (51st) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 23rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 11th The Alabama Crimson Tide Offense: Anyone that says Alabama owns the best offense in the country is not a liar; they probably are. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell now has a rushing touchdown in three-straight games and four out five, plus three or more passing touchdowns in three consecutive games. He is on fire and now the third in odds for the Heisman. Russell now has 11 passing touchdowns to two interceptions, 1,414 yards through the air, and 184 on the ground. Russell had his fewest pass attempts (22) on the season against Mississippi State but was efficient with a 72.7 completion percentage, 285 passing yards, and four total touchdowns. Georgia will be his toughest test yet, but if this is a shootout and Alabama wins, then Russell will be the favorite for the Heisman and Bama could climb as high as No. 1 or 2 in the AP Poll. The Alabama Crimson Defense: The Alabama defense may be flying under the radar this year because of how well the offense has been playing. The Tide allow 78.6 rushing yards per game (10th) due to teams falling behind and abandoning the run, rank 15th in third-down defense (27.5%), and have the seventh-best turnover margin per game (+1.4). One of the negatives has been the red zone defense, which ranks 117th with a 92.9% conversion rate — 13 out of 14 red zone opportunities have resulted in points for Alabama's opponents. That will be something to watch in this top 10 showdown. Alabama Player to Watch on Defense: DL Devan Thompkins Devan Thompkins is projected tone a first round pick and will likely be in the middle of some big third down stops. Thompson opened the year with three combined sacks, a forced fumble and recovery against Kentucky and Florida State. In the last two games, Thompkins has 1.5 TFL and no sacks, but impacted plenty of plays as a 6-foot-5 300-pounder. Georgia ranks 13th and 4th in pass and run blocking per PFF, let's see how Thompkins feels about that. picks.blurb: ‘They haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Oklahoma upsets No. 1 Texas 27-24 in Red River Rivalry TRENDING College football live updates Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Will face Reese, Dream NFL injury tracker updates Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News Zach Ragan Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will meet in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night. Georgia hasn't won a game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa since 2007. The Bulldogs will be looking to end that streak this weekend when they play on the road against the Crimson Tide. Both teams enter the game with a 5-0 record. The winner will instantly be one of the favorites to be the top overall seed in the College Football Playoff later this year. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Georgia vs Alabama ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Crimson Tide quarterback, made his prediction for the game and he thinks the outcome will be decided by just three points. McElroy has Alabama leaving Bryant-Denny Stadium with a 31-28 win. "Alabama has 13 takeaways this year," said McElroy on Tuesday . "That's top two in the sport. (Georgia QB) Gunner Stockton has thrown one interception all season, so something's got to give here. If Alabama can steal one or maybe two possessions, then that gives them a significant edge in a game that is very much a toss-up. I'm taking the Crimson Tide 31, Georgia 28. "On paper, Georgia has the much better defense. They give up less than four yards per play. That's the best in college football. But right now, they haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has offensively. (Alabama QB) Keelon Russell is playing the best football of anybody on the entire field, and Georgia's going to have to blitz, I think, to get home before he lets it go. Kirby Smart is 90-3 in his career when Georgia scores 30 or more, and we've got the Bulldogs stopping just short of that. He's also 2-7 against Alabama and 120-14 against everybody else. So it's going to be very hard to take the Bulldogs against a really improved Alabama football team in Tuscaloosa. "I also think Alabama will force a takeaway or two that will ultimately be the difference in what is a three-point game. Look, Georgia brings the better defense to Bryant-Denny on Saturday night, but I think Alabama has the edge in just about everything else. Give me the Tide, 31-28." picks.blurb: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Oklahoma upsets No. 1 Texas 27-24 in Red River Rivalry TRENDING College football live updates Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Will face Reese, Dream NFL injury tracker updates College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) runs against the Alabama Crimson Tide Owen Hillman, UGA Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 8:34 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 in SEC) face their biggest test of the season against the Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0, 3-0 in SEC). Both teams have looked like national championship contenders; inclement weather concerns persist, and Kirby Smart's record against Alabama isn't very promising. Georgia has had strong wins against everyone they've faced, winning by at least 20 against every opponent (Tennessee State, Western Kentucky, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Vanderbilt). However, Alabama has played a tougher schedule, with Eastern Carolina and Florida State as their non-conference opponents so far, and has won against now-ranked Kentucky, South Carolina, and formerly ranked Mississippi State. There's a lot of pressure for the Bulldogs to keep rolling, and considering the state of the SEC, this could decide a contestant in the SEC championship too. Georgia vs. Alabama College Football 27 simulation Result This sim was conducted with the idea that Isiah Canion, Josh Ford, and Jorden Edmonds would be out. They were all listed as questionable on the injury report. Neither team got on the board in the first quarter due to the field conditions. It wasn't until the second quarter that the Crimson Tide struck first, with Daniel Hill rushing in a touchdown from 19 yards out to make it 7-0 at 9:44. Both teams exchanged punts, then on Georgia's next drive, Peyton Woodring nailed a 39-yard field goal to make it 7-3 at 2:50. Then, 40 seconds later, Keelon Russell's pass was intercepted by Justin Williams, who ran it back 19 yards for a touchdown to give Georgia a 10-7 halftime lead. Alabama countered with a Conor Talty 40-yard field goal at 8:33 to knot it up at 10, but then Georgia went on a long drive, capped off with a Nate Frazier touchdown to make it 17-10 with 3:22 left. Conor Talty kicked another field goal, this time from 37 yards out, to make it 17-13 by 8:13 in the fourth quarter, but Gunner Stockton fired a 73-yard bomb to Sacovie White-Helton for a touchdown to make it 24-13 Georgia. Nate Frazier essentially iced the game, as he ran in his second touchdown of the day from nine yards out to make it 31-13 by 3:33 in the fourth quarter. Alabama would get a garbage-time touchdown with Keelon Russell completing a screen pass to Kaleb Edwards to reach the final score of 31-20. Alabama got one more try, but Raylen Wilson picked off Keelon Russell again on the final play. It wasn't the most glamorous win for Georgia, but they got the job done. Both Georgia and Alabama had 4.5 yards per play, and Alabama did better on third down (eight for 16) than Georgia (five for 14). However, Georgia won the turnover battle, picking off Keelon Russell twice, while the running game did the rest. Gunner Stockton was uninspiring, going 17 for 25 for 161 yards and a touchdown and no interceptions. However, Nate Frazier came through on his return, with 95 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries. The trenches helped Georgia win too. Georgia's offensive line did allow three sacks against Alabama, all by Jah-Marien Latham, but the Bulldog defensive line sacked Russell seven times, including three by Elijah Griffin and three by Josh Horton. Georgia would be 6-0 and in contention for the No. 1 seed if this were to hold in real life. Georgia would cover, considering they were 1.5-point underdogs against Alabama, and the under would hit by half a point. That would be an acceptable result for Georgia fans. The sim is 4-0 in predicting matchups, so hopefully this holds up too. This article originally appeared on UGA Wire: College Football 27 sim predicts winner, score of Georgia vs. Alabama

picks.headline: College GameDay makes picks for USC vs. Penn State whiteout
picks.blurb: The No. 19 USC Trojans enter Saturday night’s clash against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium with their College Football Playoff hopes on the line. The Trojans will play in one of their most hostile environments this season: the Nittany Lions' annual whiteout game at Beaver Stadium, which is in primetime on NBC , with kickoff scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT. The Trojans are currently the underdogs, despite the Nittany Lions suffering two straight losses to the Wisconsin Badgers and the Northwestern Wildcats. DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Trojans as 1.5-point underdogs against the Nittany Lions. That didn’t stop a majority of ESPN’s College GameDay crew from picking the Trojans to beat the Nittany Lions as a road underdog. Here’s a look at the GameDay crew’s picks. ESPN College GameDay Predictions Desmond Howard: USC Nick Saban: USC Pat McAfee: Penn State Bryce Young (guest picker): USC Kirk Herbstreit: USC Can USC Pull Off a Statement Road Win Over Penn State? Despite being underdogs and struggling on the road under coach Lincoln Riley, USC’s offense has been among the Big Ten's best this season. Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava, who is in his second season as USC’s full-time starter, enters Saturday night’s matchup against the Nittany Lions as the Big Ten’s leading passer with 1,744 yards, 15 touchdowns, and three interceptions. Two of those three interceptions came in the Trojans' last two games against the No. 13 Oregon Ducks and Washington Huskies, which could be a concern for USC’s offense against the Nittany Lions, as one turnover could be costly in a game like Saturday night’s with Penn State. The Trojans are also depleted at wide receiver, which has always been a strength of their offense under Riley. The latest season-ending injuries to Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are crushing blows to the Trojans' offense that will affect them in Saturday night’s game against USC. A pair of freshmen, wide receiver Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman, are also listed as questionable for the primetime matchup against the Nittany Lions. Their potential absence will be yet another crushing blow for the Trojans' offense. Facing such a hostile environment on Saturday night against the Nittany Lions, it’s crucial the Trojans start fast and avoid mistakes early on in the game. In their 25-21 home win over the Washington Huskies at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Week 5, the Trojans offense got off to a slow start and even trailed by 11 early in the third quarter, before scoring 15 unanswered points to win. This is something the Trojans can’t afford to let happen on Saturday night when they face the Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium. USC looks for its first win over Penn State as a member of the Big Ten, as the two last met in 2024 in Los Angeles, a game the Nittany Lions won 33-30 in overtime. home.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht is struggling
home.blurb: "Rocco Becht's sudden decline with his passing coincides directly with the loss of rising star receiver Koby Howard," McGuire told us. "Howard went down with an injury a couple of weeks ago and perhaps not so coincidentally, Becht became less effective. Not that he was lighting things up before that, but Howard was the big play guy to open things up for the rest of Becht's targets. It certainly is not a lack of chemistry as Becht's top targets are now all guys he was throwing to at Iowa State , but the efficiency is not showing. And he seems to succumb in pressure with Penn State down late in the last couple of games. His decision-making seems flawed in the crunch time, and that is worrisome." You can put the loss of Koby Howard up against the loss of Trent Mosley as a critical missing piece for each team's passing game and offense. Penn State really misses Howard. USC really misses Mosley. Finding other solutions and alternatives becomes paramount for each offense this coming Saturday. However, Jayden Maiava is definitely a better and more talented quarterback than Rocco Becht, and not by a small margin. Let's see if USC can take advantage of its clear-cut edge at quarterback. home.blurb: USC looks for redemption with a road win, something that's been an ongoing struggle for coach Lincoln Riley's teams. Wednesday's availability report gave fans an early look at which USC players will be available in the Trojans' road clash with the Nittany Lions. Thursday's report saw one change for the Trojans, as linebacker Taylor "Taybo" Johnson was listed as out. Here's a look at the latest injury report for the Trojans matchup against the Nittany Lions. The Trojans have goals to make the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history in their fifth season under Riley. Those hopes will be on the line Saturday against the Nittany Lions, as a loss likely means the Trojans would need to win out to be considered for a spot in the 12-team CFP bracket. home.headline: USC Trojans Injury Report vs. Penn State Nittany Lions
home.blurb: As the Trojans head to the East Coast, what is the latest injury news? On ESPN's College GameDay, insider Pete Thamel alluded to a few game-time decisions affecting the USC offense. USC will also be without freshman receiver Trent Mosley for the fourth consecutive game as he recovers from a knee injury. However, this could be the last week the star receiver is out of the lineup. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt had a quiet night against Washington in week 5, but the freshman receiver still leads the team in receptions and receiving yards. Tanook Hines had his best performance of the season against the Huskies when he caught five passes for 51 yards and a touchdown. And freshman Boobie Feaster is finding his rhythm in the offense. Freshman Tron Baker are also available at receiver. Freshman tight end Mark Bowman has been another instant star for the Trojans offense. He missed last week’s contest because of a hamstring injury. Bowman is listed as questionable and is one to monitor leading up to kickoff. Per Thamel, both Bowman and Mosley will be game-time decisions against Penn State. Guard Hayden Treter is doubtful after missing last week’s game. Treter suffered an injury against Oregon in week 4 and left on a cart at halftime. Kaylon Miller would continue to start if Treter is unable to go. The Trojans are thin in the interior of its offensive line and have struggled there the past two games.
